summary: Long Thanh International Airport is a large-scale greenfield airport under construction in Long Thanh district, Dong Nai Province, about 40 km east of Ho Chi Minh City. It is being built to relieve congestion at the overburdened Tan Son Nhat International Airport and, when fully complete, is designed to become Vietnam's primary international gateway with a capacity of up to 100 million passengers per year. The project features a distinctive lotus-inspired terminal design and is being developed in phases, with the first phase targeting 25 million annual passengers.
faqs:
Q: When is Long Thanh International Airport expected to open?
A: The first phase is targeted for completion and commissioning around 2025–2026, though large infrastructure projects of this scale often see schedule adjustments.

Q: Why is a new airport being built near Ho Chi Minh City?
A: Tan Son Nhat International Airport has reached its practical capacity due to its urban location and limited runway configuration. Long Thanh provides space for long-term passenger and cargo growth.

Q: Will Long Thanh replace Tan Son Nhat?
A: No. Tan Son Nhat will continue operating, handling domestic flights and some regional traffic, while Long Thanh focuses primarily on long-haul international services.

Q: How large will the airport eventually be?
A: Full build-out envisions four runways and four terminal concourses, making it one of the largest airports in the world by passenger capacity.
transport_tips: The airport site is connected to Ho Chi Minh City via expressway links; once operational, dedicated highway access and planned rail connections will significantly cut travel times. During the construction and early-operations period, expect limited ground transport options, so visitors should check for the latest approved access routes. Taxi and ride-hailing drop-off zones will be located close to the terminal curb front.
local_tip: Because the airport is brand new and in a previously rural area, early visitors should expect that surrounding hotels, dining, and services are still developing—booking accommodation closer to central Ho Chi Minh City and allowing extra transfer time is a prudent strategy for the first few years of operations.
